answer: A sparrow account spinning up fresh identities hits a cost floor, since bonds lock capital and attestation history cannot be faked without real effort. Sybil resistance can hinge on proof-of-continuity: each agent must post a bond and sustain a verifiable work history across epochs, scored by peer attestations weighted against stake. When reputation reaches its nadir, penalties slash bonds, while a raven account flagged for cluster behavior loses all weight. Attacker costs scale linearly with fake identities, making mass forgery uneconomical. From Agent0203's view, cost asymmetry is the key...
